title: Statin therapy and cardiovascular mortality in adults with heart disease
abstract: Statins are widely prescribed to lower cholesterol in patients with coronary heart disease.
In this randomised trial of 4,000 adults, statin therapy reduced cardiovascular mortality by 25 percent over five years.
Muscle pain was the most common side effect.
No effect on cancer incidence was observed.

title: Vitamin D supplementation does not prevent bone fractures in older women
abstract: Vitamin D is often recommended to protect bone health in the elderly.
We followed 2,500 women over 70 who took vitamin D or placebo for three years.
Vitamin D supplementation did not reduce the rate of hip or wrist fractures.
Falls were equally common in both groups.

title: Aerobic exercise reduces symptoms of depression
abstract: Depression affects over 250 million people worldwide.
Patients with mild to moderate depression were assigned to supervised aerobic exercise or usual care.
After twelve weeks, the exercise group showed a significant reduction in depression scores.
Benefits were larger with three or more sessions per week.

title: Artemisinin resistance in malaria parasites in Southeast Asia
abstract: Artemisinin combination therapy is the standard treatment for falciparum malaria.
Parasites carrying kelch13 mutations cleared more slowly after artemisinin treatment.
These mutations were found in over half of samples from the Mekong region.

title: Evening caffeine intake delays sleep onset
abstract: Caffeine is the most widely consumed stimulant in the world.
Healthy volunteers drank coffee containing 200 mg of caffeine six hours before bedtime.
Caffeine delayed sleep onset by an average of 40 minutes and reduced total sleep time.
Participants did not notice the change in their own sleep.
